chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Miskan, from Sa'id al-A'raj, who said:

Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام said: Whoever performs tamattu' in the months of hajj, then remains in Makkah until the hajj of the following year arrives, then upon him is the blood-sacrifice of a sheep. And whoever performs tamattu' outside the months of hajj, then resides nearby until the hajj arrives, then there is no blood-sacrifice upon him. It is only a separate hajj, and the udhiyah is only upon the people of the towns.

key_terms.أَشْهُرِ الْحَجِّ: the designated months of hajj in which hajj rites are validly undertaken
key_terms.أَهْلِ الْأَمْصَارِ: the people living in the settled towns or provinces
key_terms.تَمَتَّعَ: performed Hajj al-Tamattu' or entered into the tamattu' form of pilgrimage
key_terms.جَاوَرَ: resided nearby or remained in proximity, especially in Makkah
key_terms.حَجَّةٌ مُفْرَدَةٌ: a standalone hajj not joined to tamattu' in the legal sense
key_terms.دَمُ شَاةٍ: the sacrificial blood of one sheep due as an offering

ai.seo_question: When is a sheep sacrifice required for someone who performed tamattu' and stayed in Makkah until hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling concerning one who performed tamattu' and then remained in Makkah until a later hajj season. It distinguishes between tamattu' done within the months of hajj and outside them, clarifying when a sheep sacrifice is due and when the pilgrimage is treated as a separate hajj without such a sacrifice.
